newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo dinar black market rate down to 4 to D-mark.
newsitem.headline: Yugo dinar black market rate down to 4 to D-mark.

text.p: Yugoslavia's dinar lost more than five percent of its black market value over the Christmas and New Year holidays to stand at four to the German mark on Monday, dealers said.
Ahead of the holiday the dinar stood at 3.8 to the mark, and analysts blamed growing inflationary expectations and devaluation fears for the slide in the rate.
"Flight from dinars is the cheapest and the safest way to protect whatever you've got in the local currency," one market analyst who asked not to be named told Reuters.
Bankers insisted it was not a sudden surge in the liquidity of the banking sector that caused the dinar to slide.
On the contrary, banks faced massive withdrawal of deposits ahead of the New Year and Christmas holidays, with companies paying out salaries, one private banker said.
Pressure on the dinar intensified with traders trying to convert several days of their daily receipts into marks, the only currency widely trusted among the Yugoslavs.
Analysts said the volume of the market stayed low despite an obviously greater amount of cash in circulation.
"Even 5-10 million German marks can push the dinar either way in this market," one trader said.

Economists also cited a powerful debtor lobby as a possible cause for the dinar slide. "They incurred huge debts and now expect a one-off devaluation to erase all their liabilities," an economist who declined to be named said.

Yugoslavia's government and the central bank vowed late last year to keep the dinar stable at 3.3 to the mark in 1997. It was fixed at 3.3 after a 70 percent devaluation in November 1995. Until then it had been fixed to the mark at par.
The dinar first began to lose its year-long stability when devaluation fears mounted before November general elections.
It has also been hit by massive seven-week-old street protests by students and opposition parties over alleged vote-rigging by the ruling Socialists.
